findings.title: rawTokenId is never null-checked
findings.body: The second Objects.requireNonNull call checks grantType again instead of rawTokenId. A caller can therefore construct an AccessTokenContext with a null raw token ID. encodeTokenId then produces an ID like "onrtac:null", and getTokenContextFromTokenId returns the literal string "null" as the raw ID. The check should be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").

findings.title: isAccessTokenId does not actually verify the grant shortcut
findings.body: For an encoded ID such as "onrtac:uuid", the grant shortcut is at zero-based indexes 4..5 ("ac"), but the matcher reads items[0].substring(3, 5), which yields "ta". It also returns false when that slice equals the expected shortcut, reversing the intended condition. Consequently, the matcher returns true for any UUID-suffixed ID regardless of the encoded grant type, so integration tests will not catch wrong grant shortcut encoding. Use substring(4, 6) and return true when it equals expectedGrantShortcut.

findings.title: Grant shortcuts are not validated against the 2-character decoder contract
findings.body: postInit accepts any string returned by OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() and stores it without checking its length. The default encoder hard-codes a 6-character context (session 2 + token 2 + grant 2), and getTokenContextFromTokenId throws when the encoded context length is not 6. The SPI javadoc even says shortcuts are "usually like 3-letters", so an extension following that documentation can start successfully but produce tokens that cannot be decoded by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider. Validate that every shortcut is exactly 2 characters during postInit and fix the SPI documentation.

findings.title: Adding an abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant implementations
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is implemented by custom OAuth2 grant providers. Adding an abstract method without a default implementation means every existing external implementation must be updated before it will compile or load. If this SPI needs to remain compatible, provide a default method (for example returning a reserved/unknown shortcut) or explicitly document and handle this as a breaking SPI change.

findings.title: Incorrect-grant test passes because of an NPE, not the intended error
findings.body: before() never calls factory.postInit(), so factory.sessionFactory remains null. When getGrantTypeByShortcut looks up an unknown shortcut such as "ac", it attempts sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...) and throws a NullPointerException, which testIncorrectGrantType catches as a generic RuntimeException. The test therefore passes for the wrong reason and does not validate the real unknown-grant behavior. Initialize or mock sessionFactory and assert the expected exception type/message.
